title: Polaris quant pilot - anomaly hunt & rollout plan
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on a spike of errors in eval bucket 'B' after INT8 conversion; discussed root-cause hypotheses, perf deltas for INT8 vs FP8, rollback/fallback strategy, and an aggressive mixed-precision sweep. Agreed owners and dates for regression reruns and a limited canary rollout plan.
topics: Anomaly on NLU test bucket B
action_items: Sanjay Patel: run mixed-precision sweep (INT8/FP8 hybrid) across 3 model slices and post perf+quality table; due 2026-04-14
Priya Menon: share the exact eval prompt set and failing examples for bucket B; due 2026-04-10
Jamal Brooks: deploy logging patch to capture KV-cache warmup metrics in staging; due 2026-04-12
Liam Park: send limited canary rollout checklist and updated pricing for low-bit throughput; due 2026-04-09

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Liam Park, Sanjay Patel, Maya Chen (Redwood); Dana Ortiz, Jamal Brooks, Priya Menon (Polaris)

Summary: quick sync to triage a regression in the INT8 run and align on a safe rollout path.

[00:00:00] Liam: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda—regression findings, suspected root cause, and a canary plan. sanjay do you want to kick off with the numbers?

[00:00:22] Sanjay: yeah, sure. uh so we ran the INT8 conversion across your baseline model v3.1 and compared to fp16. overall token throughput improved ~2.6x on p4d instances, latency p50 dropped from 210ms to 82ms for typical 64-token prompts. however quality metrics—on your custom NLU eval—showed a 2.1% drop in intent accuracy in bucket B. that's the spike we want to focus on.

[00:01:05] Dana: can you repeat the bucket B note? i saw the higher error rate but didnt' realize it was that concentrated.

[00:01:10] Sanjay: yeah bucket B is basically the clinical Q/A prompts with lots of short context windows. some hypotheses: kv cache warmup, outlier tokens quantized poorly, or the hard-coded pos-emb interactions with our low-bit emulation. also might be a data-distribution mismatch where your few-shot examples are longer than the training distribution.

[00:01:45] Priya: we did notice most fails are short inputs under 32 tokens, sometimes abbreviations like 'bp' or 'hs' are mis-parsed. could that be tokenization sensitivity with int8?

[00:02:05] Sanjay: yep, tokenization plus quantization noise can amplify on rare subword combos. int8 tends to clip weight distribution; fp8 is often softer. interestingly when we ran fp8 the drop was only 0.4%. so fp8 seems closer to baseline.

[00:02:32] Jamal: can you share the exact perf numbers across the 3 slices you tested? i want latency and p99 as well, because we have SLO at 450ms p99.

[00:02:45] Sanjay: sure — quick notes: INT8 p99 was 520ms on p4d with current batching, so that exceeds SLO for some heavy tail. fp8 p99 was 360ms. throughput-wise int8 still best for cost/unit, but p99 tail for int8 is tricky — likely because of occasional cache misses we saw.

[00:03:20] Liam: so tradeoff is clear — int8 gives best tokens/sec and cost reduction roughly 38% but introduces some p99 tail and a measurable quality delta on this specific bucket. our recommended path is a hybrid: use INT8 for high-throughput non-critical routes, and fp8 or full precision for your NLU-critical endpoints, or run a canary to validate.

[00:03:45] Dana: we need a concrete rollback plan. last time we pushed low-bit across all routes and saw client complaints. we can't have that again.

[00:03:53] Maya (talking over): absolutely, we'll propose a phased canary — 2% traffic for 24 hours, monitor accuracy and p99, automatic fallback to fp8 on threshold breach.

[00:04:06] Jamal: what thresholds are we thinking? accuracy drop >0.5% or p99 > 450ms?

[00:04:14] Liam: propose both — if either threshold is hit we'll instant-failover. set accuracy delta threshold to 0.5% on the canonical eval suite and p99 threshold to 450ms.

[00:04:28] Priya: question — when you say accuracy delta, are you using strict exact-match or some fuzzy score?

[00:04:33] Sanjay: currently we reported intent accuracy exact-match. for canary we'll track intent precision/recall and also synthetic prompt-level fidelity (we call it fidelity-score). it's coarse but helps correlation.

[00:05:02] Dana: i'm worried about the 'anomaly' cases — can we identify root-cause examples so our teams can triage? we can send a labeled set.

[00:05:12] Priya: we'll extract the 120 failing samples and share by tomorrow. some are borderline, but a chunk looks like tokenization and abbreviation handling.

[00:05:25] Sanjay: great. i'll run a mixed-precision sweep: try int8 for attention/projection but keep layernorm/embeddings at fp16, and then an fp8 run. that typically recovers >60% of quality loss while keeping most perf gains.

[00:05:42] Liam: what about KV-cache warmup? you mentioned cache misses driving p99 tail — can we instrument that?

[00:05:49] Jamal: yes we can. i'll add a logging patch to capture KV-cache hit-rate and token latency distribution in staging. might add minimal overhead but should be fine.

[00:06:02] Sanjay: note — some of our int8 kernel choices in the runtime are heuristics. if the distribution of activations differs from expected, the chosen quant params can underperform. we can force re-calibration with an activation trace from your dataset.

[00:06:18] Priya: how invasive is re-calibration? we dont want it to break the model.

[00:06:22] Sanjay: it's a light-weight step — we run a small calibration set (couple hundred samples) to pick per-layer scales. non-destructive. we can do it in staging first.

[00:06:35] Dana: ok that sounds reasonable. timeline-wise what do you need from our side?

[00:06:41] Liam: priya to send failing examples, jamal to push logging, sanjay to run mixed-precision and calibration, and then we reconvene on the results. liam to send canary checklist and pricing.

[00:06:56] (brief cross-talk)

[00:07:10] Jamal: small nit — are we planning canary in us-east or eu-west? our traffic split is heavier in us-east and we want low risk.

[00:07:18] Liam: recommend starting in eu-west at 2% traffic to reduce blast radius, then expand if metrics look good.

[00:07:25] Dana: what about encryption and audit logs for the canary? our compliance requires KMS-backed keys and auditability for all production toggles.

[00:07:33] Maya: Redwood Private supports KMS and audit logs; for hosted we can enable customer-managed keys in the private control plane if you sign the addendum. i'll add the compliance doc link in the notes.

[00:07:47] Priya: do you have any numbers on cost delta if we run hybrid routes (int8 for background calls, fp8 for NLU)?

[00:07:55] Liam: rough model — hybrid gives ~24% cost reduction overall versus fp16 baseline, versus 38% if everything is int8. so we sacrifice some cost upside but keep quality. i'll share a small spreadsheet.

[00:08:12] Sanjay: also important — some degradations only show up on longer-context cases; your bucket B is short, which is odd. that suggests tokenization/embedding sensitivity rather than long-sequence artifacts.

[00:08:30] (silence, typing)

[00:08:55] Priya: quick aside — we saw a few hallucination examples that only occurred under int8; do you have guidance on which layers tend to introduce this behavior?

[00:09:03] Sanjay: hallucinations often correlate with attention projection quantization; keeping projection matrices at fp16 helps. also recomputing logits in fp32 at the end can cut spurious tokens.

[00:09:20] Dana: can we do that recompute as part of the canary?

[00:09:24] Sanjay: yes, it's a lightweight change — we can enable logit-recompute for the canary variant.

[00:09:33] Jamal: any concerns around throughput when we add logit-recompute?

[00:09:38] Sanjay: small hit ~5-8% in tokens/sec, still much better than fp16, and p99 improves because some bad tokens are avoided.

[00:09:50] Liam: okay i want to put numbers next to owners — sanjay will post a perf+quality CSV by 14th, priya will share labeled fails by 10th, jamal will push logs by 12th, and i'll send canary checklist and cost spreadsheet by 9th.

[00:10:12] (longer discussion on instrumentation details omitted for brevity)

[00:25:32] Speaker 2 (probably Mia?): can you confirm the exact hardware we used for the tests? was it p4d or v100?

[00:25:40] Sanjay: p4d. we also ran a smaller fp8 test on t4s for throughput estimates, but main numbers are p4d.

[00:26:05] Priya: is there a chance the tokenizer version mismatch could be the cause? our production tokenizer is a slightly patched tokenizer, we forgot to mention that earlier.

[00:26:14] Jamal: oh yeah we use tokenizer v2.3-patch with custom merges. that discrepancy could explain the bucket B issues.

[00:26:23] Sanjay: okay that's important — please share the tokenizer bundle and we'll re-run calibration with that exact tokenization.

[00:26:38] Dana: regarding SLOs — if we must failover, how fast is the automatic fallback? milliseconds or minutes?

[00:26:45] Liam: we have an automated route-switch that can revert traffic within ~30s, but full warmup back to stable latency might take several minutes depending on KV-cache behavior. that's why we favor small canaries.

[00:27:00] Priya: one more question on metrics — can you emit per-prompt fidelity scores to our metrics pipeline?

[00:27:06] Maya: yes we can add a fidelity metric that ships to your datadog/project monitoring. we'll include the metric name in the checklist.

[00:27:20] (short silence)

[00:27:45] Liam: quick risk register — tokenization mismatch, Kv-cache warmup, quant calibration. mitigation: share tokenizer, add kv logging, run per-layer calibration and mixed-precision sweeps.

[00:28:05] Dana: sounds good. about rollouts — will the canary be toggleable by route? we have several api routes for clinical vs background tasks.

[00:28:15] Liam: yes it's per-route; Redwood routing policies let you pin model variants per route and you can set traffic percentages.

[00:28:25] Jamal: regarding audit/compliance — maya will send the doc but we also need SAML provisioning for the staging admin if we want to review logs.

[00:28:33] Maya: noted, i'll include steps for SAML/SSO in the follow-up.

[00:28:40] Priya: timeline check — if we run the mixed-precision sweep and calibration by the 14th, when could we realistically run the canary?

[00:28:46] Sanjay: assuming results are green, we can do a 24-hour canary by 2026-04-16. gives a few days to validate and to push the small logging change.

[00:28:55] Dana: ok lock that in tentatively.

[00:29:05] (wrap-up discussion on when to schedule deep technical follow-up if issues persist)

[00:30:12] Liam: recap of next steps and owners — we'll send notes and checklist after this call. next sync in one week, or earlier if we see anomalies.

[00:30:30] Dana: thanks everyone.

[00:30:34] Jamal: thanks, bye.

[00:30:36] Priya: bye.

[00:30:38] Sanjay: thanks, bye.

[00:30:40] Liam: end meeting
